Yes! Once you create a design in our Design Lab, you can apply it to multiple product types. title: Conference Survival Guide Series: 15 Promotional Products for Making an Impression
description: Conferences are a busy environment where attendees receive many promotional items. To stand out, companies should offer unique and memorable custom promotional products that will be used during the event and long after.
content:
How Custom Ink works

This post is a playground! Everything can be edited in our Design Lab and all of the designs shown in this post are templates. You can use them as-is or add to them, adjust them, change colors, and change the product that you print them on. You can also make any order into a group order where you can share a link with your friends and family so that they can get their very own version of your great design. They can each place orders, pay, and have their items shipped directly to them. Bottom line: Have fun with it!

Conferences are not for the weak. They are a full-on onslaught of people, booths, networking, and opportunities and you have to be on your game. And people attending them get a lot of stuff. The best way to help your company stand out from the crowd is to make unique, memorable custom promotional products that they’ll actually use—at the conference and for years to come.

1 2.5″ x 2.5″ Square Business Cards ‑ 14 pt. Cardstock

The number one must have item for any conference is business cards. Making a connection is great, but if you find yourself hunting for a pen and a scrap of paper to scribble down your information, you are missing a chance at a great impression. Print some up for your booth, your team, and some for you to carry with you on the floor. We like these because of their unique square shape and thick cardstock paper.

2 1.8 oz. Clip‑N‑Go Hand Sanitizer

A strong handshake can make a solid first impression. The only trouble is, the more hands you shake, the more germs you come in contact with. Hand sanitizer is a great way to make sure you stay healthy and this one with a metal mini-carabiner can easily clip to a bag or belt loop for easy access. Be a hero and give these away to prospective clients. They’ll remember that you helped them stay healthy.

3 Slim Mint Cards

Eating on the go, drinking coffee in a cab, running between appointments can make keeping your breath fresh a challenge. These slim mint cards are easy to slip in and out of a pocket and will keep you and your clients covered all day long.

4 Stand‑Up Pocket Mirror

Hair? In place. Teeth? Clear. Nose? All set. Help them make sure they’re picture perfect on-the-go with this little mirror with a cover that turns into a stand. It’s a great addition to any travel kit.

5 SPF15 Flavored Lip Balm

Talking and traveling can really dry out your lips. Lip balm will make it into even the most discerning person’s bag, and with special features like SPF, UVA/UVB, and aloe vera, they’ll really feel like you pay attention to important details.

6 Jolt Power Bank

Power outlets can be hard to come by at a conference hotel or during any type of travel. It’s a great idea to always have an extra backup battery bank. With an aluminum case, this power bank is lightweight and easy to keep close at hand.

title: The 35 Best Fonts for Embroidery
description: Embroidery adds a professional and durable touch to custom apparel like polos and hats. This article provides a list of the best fonts for embroidery and helpful hints to optimize your designs for superior stitching.
content:
Whether you’re creating custom polos for your team, or hats that highlight your brand’s logo, embroidery is an awesome way to add an extra level of polish to your design. This stitched on style makes it easy to create professional products for any occasion and is a great way to create durable long-lasting designs.

Just like screen printing, there are some special tips and tricks to make sure your embroidered design really pops, and one of the easiest ways to do so is picking the perfect font. With so many options to choose from, it may seem hard to know where to begin, but we’re here to help!

In order to help you get the most out of your embroidered apparel, we’ve prepared this list of the best fonts for embroidery, as well as a couple helpful hints so you can create embroidered custom apparel that truly stands the test of time.

Types of Fonts

First, let’s talk about fonts. When it comes to embroidery, the simpler your font is the better. That’s why sans serif fonts work best in embroidered designs. If you’re not familiar with the difference between serif and sans serif fonts, no worries! We’ve prepared a quick primer for you: 

  1. A serif font has short lines at the ends of the letters, making it look less blocky. One of the most popular serif fonts that you might know is Times.
  2. Sans serif fonts are just that–a font “sans” or without serif. A common sans serif font is Arial.

There’s also other font categories like script, handwritten, greek, and decorative fonts, which you can see in some our examples below and categorized in our lab. Some of these fonts also work great for embroidery, but if in doubt, remember the rule, simpler is better!

Elevate Your Embroidery

When we say simple, we don’t mean boring. Embroidery looks best in designs that don’t include a lot of small details and pieces that are difficult for the needle and thread to replicate. That’s why the sans serif fonts in our examples  look so great on your embroidered gear. They use solid lines and smooth curves to create interest while avoiding little lines that add unnecessary clutter on an embroidered piece. These crisp fonts will help you create custom products your whole team will love to take with them wherever they go.

title: Local vs. Online Custom T-Shirt Printing: How to Choose the Right Option
description: This guide helps individuals and businesses decide between local and online custom t-shirt printing services. It explores the pros and cons of each option to help users make an informed decision based on their specific needs.
content:
Custom T-shirts

Local vs. Online Custom T-Shirt Printing: How to Choose the Right Option

Searching for custom t-shirts and wondering whether to find a local shop or order online? You’re not alone.

Every week we talk with thousands of group organizers, team managers, and business owners who ask the same question: is a printer down the street better than one with a full online platform? The honest answer is it depends on what you need — and this guide will help you figure that out.

We’ve spent decades helping millions of groups get their gear. That experience has shown us exactly when each option shines and where each one falls short. By the end of this guide, you’ll know how to evaluate any printing provider — local or online — and make a confident decision for your order.

In This Article

  • Local vs. Online: The Core Tradeoffs at a Glance
  • When Local Printing Makes Sense
  • When Online Printing Makes Sense
  • What to Look for in Any Custom T-Shirt Provider
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Key Takeaways

  • Local printing fits specific scenarios: Same-day pickup, viewing a physical sample before committing, or when you have an existing relationship with a trusted printer in your area.
  • Online printing wins on scale and selection: Access to hundreds of styles, reliable bulk pricing, free design tools, and nationwide delivery make it the stronger choice for most groups.
  • Quality and specs matter more than channel: Whether you go local or online, knowing what fabric weight, print method, and size range you need protects you from getting something disappointing.

Local vs. Online Custom T-Shirt Printing: The Core Tradeoffs at a Glance

Before diving into specific scenarios, it helps to understand the structural differences between local print shops and online services. Neither is objectively better — they’re optimized for different priorities.

Local print shops are small businesses, usually with one or a few production facilities. Their advantage is physical proximity: you can walk in, see materials, and pick up your order when it’s ready. Their limitations often include:

  • A smaller product catalog
  • Less standardized pricing
  • Fewer decoration method options
  • No centralized design platform
  • Quality varies widely from shop to shop, and what you get depends heavily on who’s running the press that day.

Online printing services operate at scale. Because they print millions of orders, they can offer a much wider product selection (hundreds of styles from brands like Gildan, Sport-Tek, Next Level, and Bella+Canvas), maintain tighter quality control processes, and build design tools powerful enough that anyone can create professional artwork in minutes. The tradeoff is that you’re working at a distance — you won’t hold the shirt before your order ships, and turnaround typically runs 1 to 2 weeks for standard delivery.

The table below captures the most important decision factors side by side.

One thing the table can’t capture: in our experience, the single biggest predictor of satisfaction isn’t whether you ordered locally or online — it’s whether you knew exactly what you wanted going in. That means understanding the fabric, the print method, and your timeline before placing any order.

When Local Printing Makes Sense

Local print shops serve a real purpose, and there are genuine situations where walking into a shop down the street is the right call. Understanding those scenarios will save you time and prevent costly mistakes.

You Need It Today or Tomorrow

The clearest case for a local shop is a genuine same-day or next-day emergency. If your event is tomorrow and you just realized you have no shirts, a local printer with open capacity is your fastest option. That said, “emergency” is relative: many online providers now offer rush production options with 3-day turnaround, and our own delivery options include super rush timelines for orders that need to move fast. If your event is 3+ days away, you likely have enough time to order online with rush shipping.

If you do pursue a local shop for rush work, call ahead before visiting. A shop that can theoretically turn around an order same-day is only useful if they have capacity and the right blank garments in stock. Many local shops are booked out days or weeks in advance, which means the perceived speed advantage evaporates quickly.

You Want to Feel the Fabric Before Committing

Some buyers want to hold a shirt before ordering 50 of them. That’s completely reasonable, especially for organizations ordering uniforms or apparel their team will wear every day. A local shop allows you to handle a blank sample garment, check the weight, and see how the print method looks on real fabric.

Online, that tactile experience requires a different approach. A good online provider will give you real product specs — not vague descriptions — so you can make an informed decision.

For example, when you’re choosing between a Gildan 5000 (5.3 oz., preshrunk 100% cotton jersey knit, seamless body, double-needle stitched neckline, available S–5XL) and a Port & Company PC61 Essential Tee (6.1 oz., 100% soft spun cotton, shoulder-to-shoulder taping, coverseamed neck, available S–6XL), those spec differences tell you a lot about how the shirts will feel, hold their shape, and wear over time. Knowing how to read specs is a valuable skill regardless of where you ultimately order.

You Have an Established Local Relationship

If you’ve worked with a local printer for years and trust their quality and communication, that relationship has genuine value. Institutional knowledge about your logo files, your preferred print placement, and your color standards is worth protecting. There’s nothing wrong with staying with a local provider who consistently delivers, especially for simple, recurring orders.

The challenge arises when that shop’s limitations start to show — limited product options, no group order management, manual invoicing, or inconsistent print quality over time. When any of those friction points emerge, it’s worth evaluating your alternatives.

When Online Shirt Printing Makes Sense

For most groups, online custom printing is the right choice. The reasons go beyond convenience — they get to the heart of what most buyers actually need when they think through their requirements carefully.

You’re Ordering for a Group

Group orders are where local shops tend to struggle most. Collecting 30 different sizes, managing multiple payment methods, and coordinating delivery to different addresses is a logistical headache when done manually. Online platforms handle this at scale. Our group order tools let each person in your group place their own order — choosing their size and paying directly — while everything gets printed together and shipped in one coordinated fulfillment. That feature alone has saved countless organizers hours of spreadsheet work and awkward money-collection conversations.

According to our 2026 Swag Organizer Survey, swag organizers spend nearly 10 hours per week on invisible coordination tasks — sourcing, sizing, managing budgets, and handling group logistics. Tools that automate those tasks don’t just save time; they reduce the anxiety that comes with getting a large order right for a lot of people.

You Need Variety, Not Just One Style

A local shop is constrained by what it stocks. If you want a performance moisture-wicking tee for your athletic team alongside a classic cotton option for spectators, most local shops can’t fulfill both from their own inventory without significant lead time to source blanks. Online providers maintain catalogs with hundreds of options — classic cotton, performance fabric, heavyweight streetwear, fitted women’s cuts, youth sizes, and extended sizing up to 5XL or 6XL — all on one platform.

The variety extends to decoration methods, too. Screen printing is standard almost everywhere, but embroidery, direct-to-garment printing, and specialty decoration methods vary widely by shop. Many local screen printers simply don’t offer embroidery. Online, you can choose the right method for your design — screen printing for bold graphics on cotton, embroidery for a professional polo or hat, or performance printing for polyester activewear — without switching vendors.

You Want Design Help Without Extra Cost

Most local shops require you to supply print-ready artwork files. That means knowing how to work in vector graphics software — a significant barrier if you’re not a designer. Online platforms typically include free design tools that handle this for you.

Our Design Lab gives you a full canvas to work with: thousands of design templates, a clipart library, text tools, and the ability to upload your own logo. You see exactly how your design will look on the actual product before you order. If you want human support, our team of Inkers — our in-house design experts — are available to help you refine your concept at no added charge. That combination of self-serve tools and live help is genuinely rare in local print shops, where design assistance often costs extra or isn’t available at all.

“We ordered our team shirts from CustomInk and couldn’t be happier! The product choices were great, customer service helped us make our design idea a reality and the group order option made the entire process a snap!! We couldn’t be happier and will definitely order our next custom shirts with CustomInk.”

You’re Ordering in Quantity

Bulk pricing is one of online printing’s clearest advantages. Because online providers print at volume, pricing tiers are built into every product page and calculated automatically as you adjust quantity. You see your per-shirt price drop in real time as you add more pieces — no negotiation required, no quote request, no wait for a callback.

For organizations ordering branded apparel for employee programs or company events, this transparency matters. According to our 2026 Swag Trends Survey, 62% of organizers plan to upgrade to heavyweight tees and fleece in 2026 — thicker, more premium fabrics that the people receiving them will actually keep and wear. Getting that quality at a price that works for a 50-person order requires the kind of volume-driven pricing that online providers are built for.

“Great fast service, ordered about 3 weeks out, had a rep fix the colors for me and promise me fast shipment. Arrived even sooner than expected. Great company to work with, and our second Tough Mudder with shirts from Custom Ink.”

What to Look for in Any Custom T-Shirt Provider

Whether you’re evaluating a local print shop or an online provider, the same core questions apply. Having clear answers to these before you place your order will protect you from unpleasant surprises.

Printing Methods and What They Mean for Your Design

Printing method matters because different techniques produce different results on different fabrics. The table below covers the most common methods and when each makes the most sense.

One practical note: if you’re ordering performance polyester shirts (like the Sport-Tek ST350 with PosiCharge technology), screen printing with PosiCharge-compatible inks is specifically engineered to prevent color migration — a common problem when printing on 100% polyester fabrics. That’s the kind of technical detail that separates an experienced provider from one that might not know what they’re doing on performance fabric.

Fabric Specs: Why Weight and Composition Matter

Generic product descriptions like “soft cotton tee” tell you very little. Actual fabric specifications tell you a lot. Here’s a reference for the most common custom t-shirt fabrics and what they deliver in practice.

Turnaround Time: Getting Realistic About Your Timeline

Turnaround time is where many buyers get surprised. The stated turnaround from a local shop is only as reliable as their current workload — if they’re backed up, your “one week” can easily become two or three. Online providers with production guarantees and shipping tracking give you much more visibility into when your order will actually arrive.

Standard delivery for most online orders arrives within about 2 weeks with free shipping. If you need gear faster, rush options can compress that significantly. Our delivery options page shows exact timelines for every shipping tier. The key is to start planning early — from our experience, groups that give themselves at least 2 weeks almost always receive their gear before their event with no stress. Groups that wait until a week out are the ones who end up anxious.

The data backs this up: according to the 2026 Swag Organizer Survey, 30% of swag organizers say their biggest fear is swag looking cheap — and a rushed order is one of the most common causes of quality issues, since there’s less time for review, proofing, and any necessary corrections.

Quality Assurance and Guarantees

Ask any provider — local or online — what happens if the order arrives wrong. A reputable online provider will have a clear quality guarantee. We back every order with a satisfaction guarantee: if something’s wrong, we make it right. Many local shops don’t have a formalized policy, which means resolution depends entirely on the individual owner’s willingness to fix the problem.

Before ordering anywhere, check for reviews that specifically mention what happened when something went wrong. How a provider handles problems tells you far more than reviews about orders that went perfectly.

“Every year, we create a new ‘harvest’ t-shirt for our employees to wear throughout crush. This year’s theme became ‘Keep calm and crush on.’ We had multiple color combinations and different shirt designs. CustomInk made it so easy to visualize, tweak and finalize our designs.”

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How far in advance should I order custom t-shirts?

For most groups, 2–3 weeks gives you plenty of lead time with free standard shipping. If you’re cutting it closer, we offer rush options — including our 3-day super rush — for an additional fee. Check our delivery options page for current timelines by shipping tier.

Q: Can I order just one custom t-shirt?

Many of our custom t-shirt products have low or no minimums. Check the individual product page for minimum order details, or filter the t-shirt catalog by “no minimum” to see eligible options.

Q: Are bulk discounts available for custom t-shirts?

Yes. Pricing decreases automatically as you increase quantity. You can see the per-shirt price change in real time on any product page as you adjust your quantity — no quote requests, no negotiation. The more you order, the more you save per shirt.

Q: Can members of my group pay for their own custom t-shirts?

Absolutely. Our group order feature enables each person in your group to pay separately, choose their own size, and enter their own shipping address. You control the design, and we handle the rest.

Q: Can I get design help for my custom t-shirt order?

Yes. Our team of Inkers is available to help you through every step of the design process — whether you want to start from scratch, refine existing artwork, or choose a template to build from. You can reach them by phone, chat, or email via our contact page. Design help is available at no extra charge.

Q: How is online custom t-shirt printing different from a local screen printer near me?

The core differences come down to selection, tools, pricing transparency, and group order management. A local shop may offer faster same-day pickup in an emergency, but online providers like Custom Ink offer a wider product catalog (hundreds of styles from major brands), a free design platform, automated bulk pricing, and group order tools that eliminate manual coordination. For most groups ordering custom t-shirts, the online experience is faster to set up, less work overall, and more flexible.

Q: What’s the best printing method for custom t-shirts?

It depends on your design and fabric. Screen printing is the most cost-effective method for bold, simple designs on cotton fabrics and scales well for larger quantities. Embroidery is best for logos on structured garments like polos and hats. Direct-to-garment (DTG) printing handles detailed artwork and photos on 100% cotton. For performance polyester fabrics, screen printing with PosiCharge-compatible inks is recommended to prevent color migration. Our Inkers can help you choose the right method for your specific design.

Q: Can I add names and numbers to custom t-shirts?

Yes. We offer names and numbers for team and group orders. This is popular for sports teams, family reunions, and any group that wants personalized gear without managing the customization themselves.

Q: What fabric weight should I order for custom t-shirts?

For casual everyday wear and events, a 5.3–6.1 oz. cotton tee (like the Gildan Heavy Cotton 5000 or Port & Company PC61) offers a solid, premium feel that holds its shape over time. For athletic or performance use, a 3.8 oz. polyester performance fabric (like the Sport-Tek ST350 with PosiCharge technology) is a better fit. For fashion-forward or premium branded apparel, a lighter ring-spun cotton like the Bella+Canvas 3001 (4.2 oz.) offers a softer, retail-quality feel.

Q: Is there a quality guarantee on custom t-shirts ordered online?

Yes. We stand behind every order with a money-back guarantee. If there’s a problem with your custom t-shirts — a misprint, a defect, anything that doesn’t match what you approved — we make it right. That guarantee is one of the strongest reasons to choose an established online provider over an unvetted local shop.

description: It’s so exciting to come up with the perfect holiday gift for everyone on your list–but it’s never one size fits all. So how do you find something that makes everyone feel like you picked it out just for them?
content:
It’s so exciting to come up with the perfect holiday gift for everyone on your list–but it’s never one size fits all. So how do you find something that makes everyone feel like you picked it out just for them? Go custom! Here at Custom Ink, we have so many t-shirts, accessories, face masks, and unique products that you can make one of a kind. To help you get started, below is our custom gift guide for everyone on your list.

Friends & That Special Someone

T-shirts


Keeping it classic is always a good idea–so one gift we love is a t-shirt. Personalize some for your friend group, book club, or one for your boo with a romantic saying or graphic. We have to nod to the Hanes Nano-T (it was our group tee of the year for 2019). It comes in so many great colors, is super soft and comfortable, and is available in sizes to fit everyone on your list.
 

Wine gift set


Tis the season for libations! Keep the party going well after the holidays by gifting the Laser Engraved 4 Piece Bamboo Wine Gift Set. It has a wine stopper, foil cutter, bottle opener, and pourer. Your foodie group or wine-loving friends will be so excited for this gift. And the laser engraving gives it a chic, high-end look.
 
 
 

Pom pom beanies


You can never have too many hats in the chillier months, and a pom pom beanie is the perfect accessory for matching style with function. The New Era Fleece Lined Pom Pom Beanie has heather stripes and a dual-colored pom. Its warm fleece lining will keep you warm while hunting for a Christmas tree or for smooching your love at midnight on New Year’s Eve. Give these to your group of best friends in your fave color, or put a festive graphic to represent your group’s favorite sports team.

Family

Hoodies


Receiving a hoodie for the holidays will give anyone the cozy vibes. We’d curl up by the fire in a New Era Sueded Full Zip T‑shirt Hoodie. It’s lightweight but still great for laying with your other favorite holiday apparel. It has a lived-in softness with a vintage look that anyone would be happy to get. Give these to you fam for your cookie baking contest or for gathering together to watch a holiday movie marathon.

Coasters


All the holiday celebrations mean lots of drinks around. Give a gift that’ll keep on giving long after the party is over. The Laser Engraved Black Marble and Wood Coaster Set is a classy gift, crafted from marble and wood. The laser engraving elevates the look and we could totally see your family initial or crest on these. They’re perfect for everyone to take home to be reminded of their loved ones throughout the year.
 

Wine tumblers


Sensing a theme here? We just have so many great drinkware picks this season! The Laser Etched 12 oz. Insulated Tumbler Gift Set includes four wine tumblers made from 18/8 grade stainless steel. One of these will keep your drink cold for 24 hours or if you choose to use it hot, for six hours. It even has an easy sipping push on lid for if you want to take your drinks on the go. This is a great gift to personalize with your last name or initial. We could see these at your next picnic or, if your family is outdoorsy, camping or outdoor event!

Coworkers & Gift Swaps

Watches


It seems like everyone’s got a cool watch nowadays–so make someone feel extra special and give them a watch that’s one of a kind. The Gunmetal Watch with Nylon Band is a classic style with a hint of sport thanks to the band. It’s water resistant and has a Japanese quartz movement. This would be a great choice to gift your coworkers so you can all match. Or, personalize it with an artsy design for your gift swap.
 

Scarves


Everyone is stoked when they unwrap a scarf, so imagine how great it is when it’s a custom scarf? The Sportsman Solid Knit Scarf comes in tons of great colors like pink and heather royal. It’s soft and since it’s one size fits all, it’s an easy and thoughtful gift for your group of coworkers.
 
 
 

Stuffed animals


Is there anything more “holiday” than toys? Make someone feel like a kid again by giving them a personalized Gund Baby Bear. This little guy has an embroidered nose and eyes and your design can go right on his t-shirt–which comes in a bunch of fun colors. We could see him wearing your company logo, or a funny work saying for all of your colleagues.

Employees

Wood cutting board


Show your employees you care with this sharp looking gift. The Laser Engraved Black Marble and Wood Cutting Board is such a unique pick this holiday season. It’s classic with natural materials like wood and marble, and your laser engraved logo will add extra flair. Your employees will love this gift–especially if you’re in the food or hospitality industries.
 
 

Commuter tote


We swoon for the Field & Co. 16 oz. Cotton Canvas Commuter Tote. This trendy bag has a main compartment for all your commuting necessities, with a patterned lining and a pocket to protect your laptop or tablet. The shoulder strap even adjusts to fit anyone, and the stylish colors are the perfect backdrop for your logo. Your workers will be saying “best employer ever” all year long.
 

Pen set


Something your employees will want to hold on to? The Laser Engraved Cutter & Buck Midlands Pen Set. This set has a ballpoint and a roller ball pen with black ink. The brushed nickel finish is a classic canvas for your laser engraved logo. The only issue with these is that everyone will love them so much, they’ll have to hide them in their desks to keep them from getting swiped!

Custom face masks


This year, the holidays might look a little different, but it doesn’t mean you can’t customize a thoughtful and useful gift. There’s so many different options for face masks out there, and we’re big fans of our Customized Super Comfort Cotton Face Mask. It’s lightweight, reusable, and comfortable. It has a tailored fit with adjustable ear toggles, a moldable nose bridge, and soft elastic ear loops to make it a great fit for anyone on your list. It even has an antimicrobial finish and a pocket for adding a filter. This mask really does it all and with your custom design, would make a great gift this year.

Looking for more ideas for your corporate gifts for employees, customers, or clients? Check out our Corporate Gift Guide. Who are you creating something special for this holiday season? Tell us all about it in the comments below!

title: Custom Ink’s Custom Gear Guide for Teachers & Faculty
description: Custom Ink provides a guide for teachers and faculty to create custom t-shirts and personalized gear, helping them inspire students and foster school pride. The article offers top picks and design tips for various custom apparel and accessories.
content:
Being a teacher isn’t just about lesson plans and grading–it’s about inspiring your students and rallying together to show school pride. What’s a better way to do that than with custom t-shirts and personalized gear? Custom Ink offers many great products to customize using your school colors, mascot, or classroom slogan. Whether you want to unite your classroom or the entire school, customized apparel is sure to do the trick. Below are our top picks and tricks for custom gear for teachers, faculty, and students.

Show Your Pride in Classic T-shirts 

Not sure where to begin? A t-shirt, for sure! A t-shirt is a timeless piece of swag that you’ll wear for years to come. It’s also perfect for casual Fridays or to wear to your after-school event or sports game. We can see you wearing these while chaperoning prom or a school trip! 

If you have a school logo or mascot, you can upload it right into our Design Lab and make it just right for your t-shirt design. You can even upload photos to your shirts if you want to show off your classroom or teacher’s group. We’d customize the Bella + Canvas Jersey T-shirt. It’s a premium tee with super soft cotton and comes from a brand you know and love. These classic tees come in nearly 100 colors and are available in women’s sizes so it’s perfect for your staff of any shape and size.

Customize Something the Whole School Can Wear 

In charge of creating a look your teachers, staff, and even students and parents can wear? Then keep it simple and customize something that works for everyone! Whether it’s your school name and logo in an understated design on the chest of a tee, or going for a spirited look on a sporty shirt, creating something timeless can work in so many ways. 

Give away the t-shirts at your pep rally, or start a school fundraiser. For groups, we love the Hanes Perfect-T—it comes in men’s, women’s, plus, and youth sizes, so everyone in your school can get a tee that fits them just right.

Make Use of Your School Colors and Mascot 

The best way to show your school pride? Your colors and mascot! We have shirts in so many colors it’ll be easy to find one to match yours. If you have two colors, use one as your shirt color and the other as your text and ink color. Just upload your logo or mascot into the lab and you can add text in tons of fonts, your school letters, and more. 

Don’t have a mascot logo handy? Check out our mascot templates or art in the lab to find one that works for you. We have tons to offer from bobcats to Vikings. For spirit wear, we’re really into the Sport-Tek Raglan T-shirt. It gives us all the varsity vibes and we could see it stealing the show at your next school event.

Layer With Zip-Ups 

Add some depth to your custom apparel with layering pieces. Try a classic quarter zip-up, like the Sport Tek TriBlend Quarter Zip—you’ll look great like these Global Studies teachers! Looking for something super trendy? We’re loving these OGIO Performance Zip Sweatshirts! They keep you looking so sharp and stylish and come with great features, like reflective taping and thumb holes.

 Another great option is the Champion Powerblend Quarter Zip Sweatshirt. Your staff will be so stoked to scoop one of these up. Teachers can keep them at their desks for chilly days and they’re also great for bringing outside for recess. These layering pieces would be prime items to customize as a gift for your staff! 

Stay Hydrated With Water Bottles and Tumblers

There are few things as universal as the primeval imperative to drink water, so get something everyone can use with custom water bottles and tumblers from CamelBak. Hand them out to mark the occasion for a field trip or pair it with other custom apparel to make a complete gift for teachers and faculty. 

Choose from options like the CamelBak Laser Engraved 12 oz. Insulated Tumbler to keep liquids hot or cold for long periods or the CamelBak 25 oz. Eddy Tritan Renew Water Bottle to take to and from the classroom. Whichever you choose, these premium picks will be appreciated by all!    

Come Prepared With Zip Totes

Everyone knows that teachers and faculty tend to tote around a lot of stuff for classes and activities, so help them out with custom zip totes so they can always have what they need. 

The Large Multi-Pocket Zippered Tote Bag is perfect for keeping all of the essentials organized and accessible, and the zippered main compartment keeps everything secure. For an eco-friendly option, check out the Large Recycled Poly Zippered Tote Bag, which is made from 50% recycled material an comes in 17 colors. 

Polish Your Look With Embroidered Polos 

Looking for a uniform of sorts? Polos are the way to go. If you want something nice to wear some days, or even want to customize a set of polos in a bunch of different colors for your staff, a polished look is always in style. If you want a classic polo, the Hanes EcoSmart 50/50 Jersey Polo is the choice for you. 

For something perfect for warmer months, check out the Nike Dri-FIT Micro Pique Performance Polo 2.0. We love the Nike branding on the sleeve so that it lets your logo on the front shine, plus the Dri-FIT fabric is breathable and comfy, and it’s available in women’s sizes. Matching polos would be fun for your staff for the first day of school, or as a gift for Teacher Appreciation Week.

Accessorize Your Classroom 

Who doesn’t love back-to-school shopping for notebooks, pens, and desk accessories? We sure do! But you can make it even more exciting by customizing all of your classroom gear. Design amazing signs and banners to welcome new students, celebrate Teacher Appreciation Week, and decorate for events like Ocean Week. 

Customize Moleskin notebooks for your class or school to give out to new students–you can even make your own pens to go with them! We also have sticker rolls you can personalize for your classrooms to kick off the new year, or to use for grading assignments.

Feeling inspired to customize your own gear for the school year? Head into our Design Lab to get started. Or if you want one of the products from this post, click on the link above, choose your color, and head into the lab to get started. What are you going to create for your school?

title: How Many Giveaways to Order for a Trade Show & Where to Buy: The Bulk Buyer’s Guide
description: This guide will walk you through exactly how many giveaways to order, what to budget, and how to buy affordable trade show swag that actually makes an impression. Calculating the right quantity isn’t complicated once you understand the math.
content:
You’ve booked your booth. You’ve designed your display. Now comes the question that keeps trade show first-timers up at night: how many giveaways should you actually order? Order too few, and you’ll run out by lunch on day one. Order too many, and you’re stuck storing boxes of branded stress balls in your office closet for the next three years.

At Custom Ink, we’ve helped thousands of businesses prepare for trade shows, conferences, and expos over the years, and we’ve handled it all. Calculating the right quantity isn’t complicated once you understand the math. And finding a reliable source for bulk promotional items is easier than you might think.

This guide will walk you through exactly how many giveaways to order, what to budget, and how to buy affordable trade show swag that actually makes an impression. Once you’ve got a handle on the parameters, download our free trade show giveaway calculator to determine exactly what you need and how much it will cost.

In This Article

  • The Trade Show Giveaway Quantity Calculator
  • Budget Planning for Bulk Promotional Items
  • Which Promotional Items Should Be Bought in Bulk
  • Where to Buy Promotional Items in Bulk
  • Popular Bulk Giveaways for Trade Shows
  • How to Order Bulk Trade Show Swag
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Key Takeaways

  • Plan for 15-25% of total attendees to visit your booth, then add a 10-15% buffer for day-of flexibility and post-show follow-ups.
  • Tiered giveaways work best with high-volume low-cost items for casual visitors and premium items reserved for qualified leads.
  • Bulk discounts make a real difference with significant savings starting around 50-100 units and greater discounts as quantities increase.

The Trade Show Giveaway Quantity Calculator

The anxiety around ordering the right quantity is real. We hear it from customers all the time: “What if I order 500 and only 100 people stop by? What if I order 200 and run out in two hours?” The solution is a simple formula that takes the guesswork out of the equation.

The Basic Formula

Start with the total number of expected attendees at the trade show. This number is usually published by the event organizer, or you can ask directly. According to research from the Center for Exhibition Industry Research (CEIR), approximately 16-20% of attendees will show interest in any given exhibitor’s booth. For a conservative estimate, plan for about 15-20% of total attendees to visit your booth.

For a show with 2,000 attendees, that means roughly 300-400 people could reasonably stop by your booth. But not everyone who walks past will engage deeply enough to warrant a giveaway. A more targeted approach accounts for three tiers of engagement:

  • Casual passersby (60-70% of booth visitors): These folks grab a quick giveaway and keep moving. Low-cost items like pens, stickers, or candy work perfectly here.
  • Interested prospects (20-30% of booth visitors): They stop for a conversation, take your brochure, and might scan their badge. Mid-tier items like can coolers or tote bags reward their engagement.
  • Qualified leads (5-10% of booth visitors): These are the gold. They schedule demos, exchange business cards, and show real buying intent. Premium items like quality custom t-shirts or tech accessories make sense here.

Running the Numbers: A Real Example for Buying Giveaways in Bulk

Consider a regional industry conference with 1,500 attendees. Using our formula:

  1. Estimate booth visitors: 1,500 × 20% = 300 visitors
  2. Add a buffer (15%): 300 × 1.15 = 345 potential giveaways needed
  3. Break down by tier:
    • Low-cost giveaways: 345 × 65% = ~225 items (pens, mints, stickers)
    • Mid-tier giveaways: 345 × 25% = ~85 items (koozies, bags)
    • Premium giveaways: 345 × 10% = ~35 items (t-shirts, power banks)

This tiered approach means you’re not handing a $15 t-shirt to someone who glanced at your booth for two seconds, but you do have something special for the prospect who spent 20 minutes in a serious conversation with your sales team. (Download our free trade show giveaway calculator)

  • Pro tip: Add 10-15% extra to your estimates for post-show follow-ups. Mailing a branded item with a thank-you note keeps your company top of mind after the event ends.
  • Budget tip: If you’re attending multiple shows in a year, order higher quantities upfront. The per-unit cost drops significantly with larger orders, and most promotional items don’t expire.
  • Don’t forget: Factor in items for your own staff. Your team of five needs shirts too, and having extras on hand for last-minute additions or replacements saves stress.

“Annual academic mini-conference that’s organized entirely by an interdisciplinary group of graduate students from UC Berkeley and Stanford. These can-coolers kept our beverages cold and our hands warm while also sparking conversation and excitement about Microbiology during the post-symposium rooftop reception!”

— Christopher Gee, Microbiology Student Group

Budget Planning for Bulk Promotional Items

Understanding costs upfront prevents sticker shock and helps you allocate your trade show budget wisely. The average cost of trade show displays and swag varies widely depending on your goals, but we can break down what to expect at each price tier.

Cost Per Item by Category

Promotional product pricing depends on the item type, customization complexity, and order quantity. According to the Advertising Specialty Institute (ASI), promotional products deliver one of the lowest costs per impression of any advertising medium, often as low as 1/10 of a cent per impression. That’s because recipients keep useful items for months or even years, generating ongoing brand exposure.

  • Budget tier ($0.50-$2 per item): Pens, stickers, buttons, mints, and small magnets. Perfect for high-volume giveaways where you need hundreds of items.
  • Mid-range tier ($2-$8 per item): Can coolers, tote bags, sunglasses, basic drinkware, and lanyards. These offer good perceived value without breaking the budget.
  • Premium tier ($8-$25+ per item): Custom t-shirts, quality water bottles, power banks, Bluetooth speakers, and premium bags. Reserve these for qualified leads and VIP contacts.

Sample Budget Breakdown

For a booth expecting 400 visitors using the tiered approach:

  • 260 budget items at $1.00 each = $260
  • 100 mid-tier items at $4.00 each = $400
  • 40 premium items at $18.00 each = $720
  • Total promotional product budget: approximately $1,380

This approach ensures you have plenty of items for high-traffic moments while reserving your best trade show giveaways for the prospects most likely to convert.

  • Budget tip: Bulk discounts can reduce per-unit costs by 20-40% compared to smaller orders. Our pricing automatically adjusts as you increase quantities in the cart.
  • Shipping note: We include free standard shipping on all orders, so factor that savings into your budget. Many competitors charge separately for shipping, which can add significant costs to bulk orders.

“We are a small team from a tech startup and this was our first trade show. We looked like a cohesive team and got a lot of traction at the show.”

Which Promotional Items Should Be Bought in Bulk

Not everything belongs in a bulk order. Some products deliver excellent value at higher quantities, while others work better in limited runs. After years of helping businesses stock their trade show booths, we’ve seen clear patterns in what works.

Best for High-Volume Bulk Orders

These items offer the best per-unit economics at scale:

  • Drinkware: Can coolers and basic tumblers are trade show staples. They’re lightweight, easy to distribute, and get used repeatedly. ASI research shows drinkware generates an average of 1,400 impressions over its lifetime.
  • Tote bags: Attendees use them to carry materials around the show floor, providing walking advertisements for your brand. They also get reused for shopping and everyday errands long after the show ends.
  • Pens and writing instruments: The workhorse of promotional products. Inexpensive per unit, useful to everyone, and easy to distribute quickly during busy periods.
  • Stickers and buttons: Perfect for younger audiences or creative industries. Minimal cost at high volumes with strong brand visibility.

Better for Limited Quantities

These items make more sense as targeted giveaways for qualified leads:

  • Apparel: T-shirts, polos, and hoodies are popular but require size variety. They work best as premium giveaways for engaged prospects or as team uniforms rather than mass giveaways.
  • Tech accessories: Power banks, USB drives, and wireless chargers have higher perceived value. Reserve them for leads who complete product demos or schedule follow-up meetings.
  • Premium drinkware: Quality stainless steel tumblers or branded bottles work as high-value giveaways for VIP contacts and serious prospects.
  • Strategy tip: Use premium items as incentives for specific actions. “Complete our product demo and receive a free power bank” drives engagement better than just handing items out freely.
  • Storage consideration: High-volume bulk items should be easy to store. Flat-packed items like koozies and tote bags take up far less space than bulky tech gadgets.

Where to Buy Promotional Items in Bulk

Finding the best suppliers for custom conference swag requires balancing price, quality, and reliability. The cheapest option isn’t always the best value, especially when late delivery or poor print quality can damage your brand image at a major event.

What to Look For in a Supplier

  • Transparent pricing: Avoid suppliers with hidden fees for setup, artwork, or shipping. Your quoted price should be your final price.
  • Guaranteed delivery dates: Trade shows don’t wait. Make sure your supplier can meet your deadline with time to spare.
  • Quality samples: Order samples before committing to large quantities. The $20 spent on samples can save thousands on a disappointing bulk order.
  • Design support: Even if you have a logo file, expert eyes can catch issues that affect print quality before production begins.
  • No or low minimums: Flexibility matters, especially for premium items where you only need a few dozen units.

Why Customers Choose Custom Ink for Their Trade Show Giveaways

Custom Ink has been helping businesses create custom promotional products for over two decades. Thousands of companies have trusted us with their trade show swag, corporate gifts, and employee apparel. A few things set us apart:

  • Free standard shipping on all orders eliminates one of the biggest surprise costs in promotional product ordering. Your quoted price is your final price.
  • Our Design Lab makes it easy to upload your logo, see exactly how it will look on different products, and make adjustments in real time. No design skills required, but our team of Inkers is available if you want expert help.
  • Bulk discounts kick in automatically as you increase quantities. Add items to your cart and watch the per-unit price drop. For very large orders, contact our team directly for custom quotes.
  • Real people answer the phone seven days a week. Whether you have questions about product selection, design adjustments, or delivery timing, you can talk to someone who can actually help.

How to Order Bulk Trade Show Swag

Ordering promotional products for your trade show doesn’t have to be complicated. Follow these steps to get your bulk order placed and delivered on time.

  1. Calculate your quantities using the formula above. Estimate booth visitors, break down into tiers, and add your buffer.
  2. Choose your products from our promotional products catalog. Consider a mix of price points for different engagement levels.
  3. Upload your logo to our Design Lab. You can also start with a template or work with our design team.
  4. Preview your design on each product. Make sure colors look right and your logo is properly sized.
  5. Select quantities and sizes for each item. Watch the per-unit price drop as you increase quantities.
  6. Choose your delivery date. Standard shipping is free and arrives within two weeks. Rush options are available for faster turnaround.
  7. Review and place your order. Our team checks every design before printing and will contact you if we spot any issues.

  • Don’t forget: Have your logo file ready in a high-resolution format. Vector files (AI, EPS, PDF) work best, but we can also work with high-resolution PNG or JPG files.
  • Need help? Call us at 800-293-4232 or start a live chat. Our team can help with product recommendations, design questions, and bulk order quotes.

Q: How many promotional items should I order for a trade show?

Plan for 15-20% of total show attendees to visit your booth, then add a 10-15% buffer. For a 2,000-attendee show, that means approximately 350-450 giveaway items. Consider tiering your giveaways with high-volume budget items for casual visitors and premium items reserved for qualified leads.

Q: Are there minimum order requirements for bulk promotional items?

Many of our promotional products have no minimum order requirements. Some items do have minimums, which are clearly displayed on each product page. You can filter by “no minimum” when browsing to find products that work for smaller quantities.

Q: How far in advance should I order trade show giveaways?

We recommend ordering at least three weeks before your event for standard shipping. Four to six weeks provides a comfortable buffer for large orders or if you need time for design revisions. Rush options are available and can get your order to you in as few as three days for an additional charge. View our delivery options for details.

Q: Are bulk discounts available for promotional products?

Yes, per-unit prices drop as quantities increase. Bulk discounts typically become meaningful starting around 50-100 units per item. Add items to your cart in our Design Lab and adjust quantities to see how pricing changes. For very large orders, contact our team for custom quotes.

Q: What are the most cost-effective promotional items for trade shows?

Pens, can coolers, and tote bags offer excellent value at higher quantities. These items provide low cost-per-impression because recipients keep and use them repeatedly. According to ASI research, promotional products can deliver cost-per-impressions as low as 1/10 of a cent.

Q: Can I mix different products in one order for trade show swag?

Yes, you can include multiple product types in a single order. This makes it easy to order your tiered giveaways together. Each product can have the same logo or different designs based on your needs.

Q: Can I get help designing my promotional products?

Absolutely. Our design experts (we call them Inkers) are available to help you create the perfect design at no extra cost. You can also use our Design Lab templates and clipart library to build designs on your own. Call us at 800-293-4232 or start a live chat for design assistance.

Q: What’s the average cost of trade show promotional items?

Costs vary widely by product type. Budget items like pens and stickers run $0.50-$2 per item. Mid-range products like koozies and tote bags typically cost $2-$8 each. Premium items like custom t-shirts and tech accessories range from $8-$25+ per item. Quantities significantly affect pricing, with bulk orders reducing per-unit costs by 30% or more.

Q: Is shipping included in the price for bulk promotional items?

We include free standard shipping on all orders. The price you see in your cart is the price you pay. No hidden fees for shipping, setup, or artwork. Rush shipping is available for an additional charge if you need faster delivery.

Q: What file format do I need for my company logo on promotional products?

Vector files (AI, EPS, SVG, or PDF) work best for printing. High-resolution PNG or JPG files (300 DPI or higher) also work well. Our design team reviews every order and will contact you if your artwork needs adjustment for optimal print quality.

title: Which Hat Customization Method is Best? Embroidery vs. Screen Printing vs. Patches
description: When you’re creating custom hats for your team, business, or event, choosing the right decoration method makes all the difference. Embroidery, screen printing, and patches each bring something unique to the table, and understanding how they work with different hat styles and materials will help you get exactly what you’re looking for.
content:
When you’re creating custom hats for your team, business, or event, choosing the right decoration method makes all the difference.

Embroidery, screen printing, and patches each bring something unique to the table, and understanding how they work with different hat styles and materials will help you get exactly what you’re looking for.

We’ve helped millions of groups find their perfect custom headwear, and we’ve learned a lot along the way about what works best for different situations.

In This Article

  • Understanding Hat Customization Methods
  • Embroidery: The Gold Standard for Custom Hats
  • Screen Printing: Vibrant, Colorful Hat Designs
  • Patches: The Trending Dimensional Look
  • Matching Decoration Method to Hat Material
  • How to Choose the Right Method for Your Project
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Key Takeaways

  • Embroidery is the gold standard for most custom hats, providing a durable 3D texture that looks professional and holds up to years of wear.
  • Screen printing excels on foam-front trucker hats when you have colorful, detailed designs that would lose clarity in stitched form.
  • Patches offer retail-quality dimension with options including embroidered, leather, PVC, and woven styles that give hats a premium, trendy look.

Understanding Hat Customization Methods

Choosing the right customization method is about more than just aesthetics. The decoration you pick affects durability, cost, design possibilities, and how the finished hat looks on different materials.

We offer three main approaches:

  1. Embroidery (stitching thread directly into the fabric)
  2. Screen printing (applying ink through mesh screens)
  3. Patches (attaching pre-made decorative elements).

Each has strengths that make it ideal for certain situations.

Over the years, we’ve noticed that customers who understand these differences end up happier with their final products. A detailed multi-color logo might look stunning screen printed on a trucker hat but would need to be simplified for embroidery.

Similarly, a simple text design that would look crisp embroidered might appear flat when screen printed. The key is matching your design to the right method and the right hat.

Before you commit to a decoration method, explore our complete overview of custom hat styles to ensure you’re choosing the right base product.

“14 adults and 17 kids, 3 nights sleeping in tents… priceless! Thanks to Custom Ink, we could keep track of our whole crew!”

Embroidery: The Gold Standard for Custom Hats

Embroidery is what most people picture when they think of custom embroidered baseball caps. It’s the process of stitching thread directly into the hat fabric using computerized embroidery machines. The result is a textured, three-dimensional design that looks and feels premium. There’s a reason embroidery remains the most popular choice for professional sports teams, corporate branding, and organizations that want their hats to make a lasting impression.

From our experience helping thousands of teams and businesses, embroidery consistently delivers when durability matters. The stitched design won’t crack, peel, or fade the way printed designs sometimes can. Embroidered hats hold up to sun exposure, rain, and regular washing without losing their crisp appearance. For groups ordering hats they’ll wear season after season, embroidery is the clear winner for longevity.

Best Uses for Embroidery

  • Corporate logos and company branding: The professional, polished look of embroidery builds brand credibility. Learn more about how businesses leverage branded headwear to build both team unity and brand recognition.
  • Sports teams and athletic organizations: Durable enough for active wear and outdoor conditions
  • Workwear and uniforms: Withstands daily use without deteriorating
  • Golf outings and outdoor events: Looks sharp while standing up to weather
  • Simple text and clean logo designs: Bold lines and shapes translate beautifully to stitches

Hat Design Considerations for Embroidery

Not every design works equally well for embroidery. The process converts your artwork into stitches, so very fine details, tiny text, or gradients can lose clarity. We recommend keeping designs relatively simple with clean lines and solid colors. Text should be at least a quarter-inch tall to remain legible, and intricate details smaller than about an eighth of an inch may not translate well.

One thing we’ve learned helping customers over the years: simpler designs often look more impressive when embroidered. A bold logo with two or three colors will pop beautifully with that dimensional texture. If you have a complex design, our team of Inkers can help you adapt it for embroidery while keeping the essence of your original artwork intact.

“Our soccer team, the Blue Sharks, are comprised of buddies who have known each other since they were toddlers. This is our second season together and last year we made custom t-shirts for the boys and parents. So for this season we decided to make personalized embroidered caps and we went to CustomInk to accomplish this. It’s been an absolute pleasure working with the CustomInk team and from the looks on the boys’ faces when we handed them out at practice, they’re very happy as well.”

Design Templates for Embroidered Hats

Screen Printing: Vibrant, Colorful Hat Designs

Screen printing on hats works differently than on t-shirts, and it’s available on specific hat styles designed to take ink well. The process pushes ink through a mesh screen onto the hat’s surface, creating a smooth, flat design. Trucker hats with polyester foam fronts are particularly well-suited for screen printing because the foam provides a stable, smooth surface that holds ink beautifully.

We carefully test all our hats before adding them to the site to ensure screen printing produces great results. If you’re looking for hats available for screen printing, you can filter our selection by decoration type. The result is a thick, vibrant print with colors that really pop. For designs with lots of detail or multiple colors that might get lost in embroidery stitches, screen printing captures every nuance.

Best Uses for Screen Printing

  • Multi-color designs and detailed artwork: Each color can be reproduced with precision
  • Promotional giveaways and events: Cost-effective for larger quantities
  • Casual and fun designs: Perfect for parties, reunions, and informal gatherings
  • Designs with fine details: Small text and intricate elements stay crisp
  • Budget-conscious orders: Often more affordable than embroidery for larger runs

Screen Printing Limitations for Hats

Screen printing works on specific hat materials, primarily foam-front trucker hats. It’s not available on cotton baseball caps, beanies, or performance hats where the fabric texture wouldn’t hold ink properly. The print is also less dimensional than embroidery. It sits flat on the surface rather than adding texture. For some designs that’s exactly what you want, but if you’re after that raised, textured look, embroidery or patches will serve you better.

Durability is good but not quite at the embroidery level. Screen printed designs can last for years with proper care, though they may eventually show wear with heavy use. For hats that will see occasional use at events or casual wear, screen printing holds up great.

“First place winners showing off their custom hats at the first annual Escape to the Coast Roller Derby tournament in San Luis Obispo, Ca! We love how they turned out and will definitely be placing future orders with CustomInk!”

Design Templates for Screen Printed Hats

Patches: The Trending Dimensional Look

Patch hats have exploded in popularity, and it’s easy to see why. A well-designed patch gives hats a retail-quality, outdoorsy aesthetic that feels premium and on-trend. We offer multiple patch types including embroidered patches, leather patches, PVC patches, and woven patches. Each provides a distinct visual and tactile effect that can make your custom hats stand out.

For detailed information on patch materials, application methods, and which hat styles work best with patches, read our comprehensive patch hats guide.

From our experience working with groups ordering custom headwear, leather patches have become particularly popular. They bring a rugged, authentic vibe that works beautifully for outdoor brands, craft breweries, adventure groups, and anyone wanting that outdoorsy aesthetic. The patches are securely stitched or bonded to ensure edge clarity and durability against sun and weather exposure.

Types of Patches Available

  • Embroidered patches: Classic look with raised thread texture, great for detailed logos and colorful designs
  • Leather patches: Premium, rustic feel perfect for outdoor brands and craft businesses
  • PVC patches: Durable rubber-like material with a modern, clean look that resists weather
  • Woven patches: Finer detail than embroidery with a smooth, flat surface for intricate designs

Why Patches Work for Custom Hats

Patches give you the dimensional look of embroidery with some added benefits. The patch can be created with finer detail than direct embroidery since it’s manufactured separately before being attached. You can also mix hat styles within the same order. Want to offer trucker hats, snapbacks, and beanies all with the same patch design? That’s possible with patches in a way that wouldn’t be practical with direct decoration.

The standard turnaround for patch hats is 10 to 14 business days after proof approval, with rush options available for tighter deadlines. The patches are either securely stitched or bonded to ensure they stay put through regular wear.

“We were having our 20 years class reunion during the whole weekend. We planned for a getaway at our favorite beach spot so I decided to commemorate the reunion with awesome hats. When my classmates got their hat, they were all in awe!! It was definitely the highlight of the event.”

Matching Decoration Method to Hat Material

Different hat materials work better with different customization methods. Understanding these pairings will help you get the best results for your project. We’ve worked with enough custom orders to know which combinations produce the most professional-looking finished products.

Cotton and Twill Baseball Caps

Cotton and twill baseball caps are the classic choice for embroidery. The woven fabric provides a stable base that holds stitches beautifully, and the structured crown gives embroidered designs a clean backdrop. Bio-washed cotton has a soft, broken-in feel right out of the box while still taking embroidery well. Twill weave fabrics are slightly more durable and hold their shape better over time.

Best decoration methods: Embroidery, patches

Foam-Front Trucker Hats

The polyester foam front panels on trucker hats provide the ideal surface for both screen printing and embroidery. The foam is stable enough to hold stitches but also smooth enough to accept ink evenly. The mesh back keeps these hats breathable for warm weather wear. If you want a printed design with lots of colors or fine detail, foam-front truckers are your go-to option.

Best decoration methods: Screen printing, embroidery, patches

Knit Beanies

Beanies made from acrylic, wool, or fleece-lined materials work exclusively with embroidery. The knit construction doesn’t support screen printing, but embroidered logos look fantastic on the cuff area. The key is keeping designs relatively compact to fit the available embroidery area. We’ve seen great results with simple logos and text on beanies for winter sports teams, outdoor organizations, and corporate cold-weather gear.

Best decoration method: Embroidery

“Members of the Jackson Hole Land Trust staff volunteered for the Salvation Army and sported our new CustomInk hats while bell ringing to raise money for a great cause. The hats kept us warm and toasty and arrived just in time for the event! We had a great experience working with the CustomInk team and will definitely use them again in the future!”

Performance and Athletic Hats

Performance hats made from moisture-wicking polyester blends are designed for athletic use. These fabrics handle embroidery well, and the professional look of stitched logos fits the athletic aesthetic. Premium brands like Nike, Adidas, and Under Armour offer performance hats that look great with embroidered team or company logos.

How to Choose the Right Method for Your Project

Selecting the right customization method comes down to a few key questions. Here’s a quick guide to help you decide:

Choose Embroidery When:

  • You want a professional, premium look
  • Durability is a priority
  • Your design has clean lines and limited colors (1-4)
  • You’re ordering cotton, twill, or performance fabric hats
  • The hats will see heavy use or outdoor wear

Choose Screen Printing When:

  • Your design has many colors or fine details
  • You’re ordering foam-front trucker hats
  • Budget is a significant consideration
  • You want vibrant, eye-catching colors
  • The hats are for casual use or promotional giveaways

Choose Patches When:

  • You want that trendy, retail-quality look
  • You need to mix hat styles in one order
  • Leather or specialty materials fit your brand
  • Your design requires finer detail than direct embroidery allows
  • You’re going for an outdoorsy, craft, or vintage aesthetic

How to Create Your Custom Hats

  1. Browse our hat selection and filter by style, color, or decoration type
  2. Start designing in the Design Lab by uploading your logo or using our clipart and font library. Our complete guide to designing custom hats covers everything from choosing the right hat style to uploading artwork and finalizing your order.
  3. Preview your design in 3D to see exactly how it will look on your chosen hat
  4. Select sizes and quantities for your group
  5. Review your proof from our expert artists before production begins

Need help deciding? Our design experts are available seven days a week to answer questions and make recommendations based on your specific project. Contact us anytime.

Whether you’re outfitting a sports team, promoting a business, or celebrating a special occasion, we have the hats, decoration methods, and expertise to help you create something your group will be proud to wear. With options ranging from premium New Era hats to budget-friendly trucker caps, and decoration methods from classic embroidery to trendy leather patches, your perfect custom hat is just a few clicks away.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is the best customization method for custom hats?

Embroidery is the gold standard for most custom hats, providing a durable, 3D texture that looks professional. Screen printing is best for foam-front trucker hats when you have colorful or detailed designs. Patches offer a trendy, retail-quality look with options including leather and PVC.

Q: What materials are best for custom hats?

Cotton and twill fabrics work best for embroidered custom hats. Polyester foam fronts on trucker hats are ideal for screen printing. Acrylic and wool beanies take embroidery beautifully. The best material depends on your intended use and desired look.

Q: How far in advance should I order custom hats?

Most custom hat orders arrive within 2 weeks with free standard shipping. Rush options are available for tighter deadlines. We recommend ordering at least two weeks ahead to allow time for design review and production. Learn more about delivery options.

Q: Can I order just one custom hat?

Many hat styles have low or no minimums. Use the “no minimum” filter when browsing to find hats available in quantities of one. Keep in mind that per-item pricing is typically lower with larger orders.

Q: Will embroidery or print hold up to regular wear and washing?

Yes, we use durable materials and stitching techniques to help your custom hats hold up over time. Embroidery is particularly durable and won’t crack, peel, or fade. Follow care instructions to extend your hat’s life.

Q: Can I get help designing my custom hat?

Absolutely! Our design experts (we call them Inkers) are available seven days a week to help you create the perfect design. You can also use the Design Lab templates and clipart to get started. Every order includes a proof review by our expert artists. Contact us for personalized help.

Q: Can members of my group pay for their own custom hats?

Yes! You can set up a group order that lets each person pay separately and specify their own size and shipping address. It’s a convenient way to coordinate orders for teams, clubs, or events.

Q: What patch types are available for custom hats?

We offer multiple patch types including embroidered patches, leather patches, PVC patches, and woven patches. Each provides a distinct visual and tactile effect. You can even mix hat styles with the same patch design in one order.

Q: Do you offer custom New Era hats?

Yes! We proudly offer a variety of New Era hats, including the highly sought-after New Era 9FIFTY Flat Bill Snapback Hat. New Era hats are beloved for their quality and we’re happy to offer this premium brand for custom embroidery.

Q: Are bulk discounts available for custom hats?

Yes, the more hats you order, the lower your price per hat. Check the product details or change the order quantity to see product-specific pricing. Our all-inclusive pricing shows you the total cost upfront with no hidden fees.
